Q: Does JS usage affect my website's security A:

If you're doing your API calls directly from the browser using frontend JavaScript, you have a major security hole.

Anything in your frontend JS is public. If your API keys are in your code, anyone can find them in seconds using the "Inspect Element" tool.

Public vs. Private:

Client-Side (Frontend JS)
- Publicly visible to everyone
- NEVER put secrets, private keys, or admin credentials here
- Anyone can read, modify, or replay these requests

Server-Side (Node.js, Python, Go, etc.)
- Hidden from the user
- This is where API keys and secrets live
- Use this as a "Proxy" to talk to your SMS or Payment providers

How to fix this:

Instead of calling the SMS API directly from the browser, do this:

  1. Client: sends a request to your server (e.g. /api/send-sms)

  2. Server: your server receives the request, injects the secret API key (stored in an .env file), and calls the actual SMS provider

  3. Security: the user only ever sees your internal URL, never your actual secret keys

Immediate risks:

  • SMS/Payment APIs: if someone finds your key, they can use your balance to send spam or fraudulent transactions

  • Auth services: if you expose admin-level keys, attackers can modify your user database

Q: Embedding the Speco webcam video into our website A:

You generally cannot embed that directly because Speco Technologies IP camera streams use proprietary ActiveX or RTSP formats that convert it to MJPEG/HLS (via VLC/FFmpeg or the camera’s settings), and then embed that stream in your ASPX page.

Q: How should I plan and structure a web app with booking and payment features as a beginner? A:

Start with the core flow (don’t think tech first)

Before stack/architecture, define:

User → selects service → chooses time slot → books → pays → gets confirmation

That’s your entire system. Everything else supports this.

Break the app into simple parts

As a beginner, keep it very basic:

  • Frontend → forms + booking UI

  • Backend (Django) → handles logic (booking, auth, payments)

  • Database → users, bookings, payments

You don’t need microservices or anything complex.

Basic backend structure (Django)

Think in terms of models:

class Booking(models.Model):
    user = models.ForeignKey(User, on_delete=models.CASCADE)
    date = models.DateTimeField()
    status = models.CharField()  # pending, confirmed

class Payment(models.Model):
    booking = models.OneToOneField(Booking, on_delete=models.CASCADE)
    amount = models.DecimalField(...)
    status = models.CharField()  # pending, paid

API design (keep it simple)

You don’t need many endpoints:

  • POST /bookings/ → create booking

  • POST /payments/ → initiate payment

  • GET /bookings/ → view bookings

Payment flow (IMPORTANT)

Don’t build your own payment system.

Use something like:

  • Stripe

  • Razorpay

Beginner-friendly stack

  • Backend: Django + Django REST Framework

  • Frontend: simple HTML / React (optional)

  • Payments: Stripe / Razorpay

  • Deployment: Render / Railway

First build it without payment and then test fully, only proceed f youre confident.

If you get stuck while implementing (especially booking logic or payment integration), feel free to reach out — I’ve worked on similar Django setups. Best of Luck!
